title: History Manager / Job Manager / Event Bus
summary: Built a unified Job state machine (QUEUED/RUNNING/COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED) with real queueing and resume, a synchronous in-process Event Bus that Collector/Parser/Rule/Report/History now all publish onto instead of calling each other directly, and a History Manager that ties per-run archival (already mostly built by the pre-existing RunManager) together with Phase 4's structured logs so a job's CLI/report/snapshot/log artifacts land in one archived unit per customer/profile/job.

changes.before: engine/history.py only ever stored scored/findings JSON per lab_name (history/<lab_name>/<session>.json) -- no archiving of raw CLI, reports, or config snapshots at all. Separately, engine/run_manager.py (pre-existing, not documented in earlier phase reports) already created runs/<run_id>/{raw,masked,parsed,analysis,reports,exports}/ per customer/profile and could move a whole run to archive/<run_id>/ via storage_service.archive_run() -- but nothing tied that to the app-level structured logs (logs/structured_<date>.jsonl) living outside the run folder, and nothing exposed a combined active+archived history view.
changes.after: New core/history_manager.py::HistoryManager.archive_completed_run(customer, profile, run_id, job_id) reads logs/structured_*.jsonl, pulls out every event matching that job_id, writes them into the run folder as logs/structured_events.jsonl, then calls the existing run_manager.archive_run() to move the whole folder (raw CLI + reports + config snapshots + now the job's logs) into archive/ as one unit. list_history(customer, profile) merges live runs/ entries with archive/ entries (reading session.json directly from each archive folder) into one chronological list. Publishes 'history.archived' onto the Event Bus. Exposed via api/grade_api.py::list_grade_history().
changes.validated: Manually verified: created a real run under data/acme/siteA, wrote a structured log event tagged with a job_id, called archive_completed_run() -- confirmed logs/structured_events.jsonl landed inside the archived folder, and list_history() correctly showed the run as archived=True in the combined list.

changes.before: Three disconnected, partial job-tracking mechanisms: api/job_runner.py (idle/running/done/error, one slot per 'kind', a second submit is silently dropped -- no real queue, no Queued state), engine/run_manager.py (READY/RUNNING/PAUSED/FAILED/ABORTED/COMPLETED -- a real state machine with resume/retry, but scoped to one Run per (customer,profile), not a general job concept), and api/terminal_inspection_api.py (a bespoke cancel_requested flag specific to one feature). No unified Queued/Cancelled states existed anywhere; grep confirmed zero prior 'queue'/'queued' usage in the whole codebase.
changes.after: New core/job_manager.py::JobManager -- single background worker thread pulling from a real queue.Queue, so submitting job 2 while job 1 runs actually queues it (QUEUED) instead of being dropped. States: QUEUED -> RUNNING -> {COMPLETED|FAILED|CANCELLED}. cancel(job_id): immediate for QUEUED, cooperative (job.cancel_requested flag + fn must raise CancelledError) for RUNNING. resume(job_id): only valid from FAILED/CANCELLED, re-submits the same fn/args as a new job (does not mutate history -- old job record stays as-is for audit). Every transition publishes onto the Event Bus (job.queued/started/completed/failed/cancelled). Wired into a real caller: api/grade_api.py::run_grade_async() runs grading through JobManager instead of blocking the pywebview bridge thread, and on completion (customer/profile mode) automatically hands the just-created run to HistoryManager.archive_completed_run(). The original synchronous run_grade() is left untouched for backward compatibility.
changes.validated: Manually verified: (1) submitted two 'grade'-kind jobs back-to-back -- both ran (second queued, not dropped); (2) cancelled a running job mid-execution -- transitioned to CANCELLED, and the already-queued second job still ran to COMPLETED; (3) called resume() on the cancelled job -- it re-ran as a new job_id and reached COMPLETED.

changes.before: Zero pub/sub mechanism anywhere in the codebase (grep for EventBus/pub_sub/publish/subscribe/on_event: no matches). pipeline/pipeline.py::Pipeline had exactly one coarse callback (on_step(name, phase)) -- not a bus, and stages still communicated by direct method calls / a shared mutable SessionContext.data dict. Collector -> Parser -> Rule -> Export -> GUI had no decoupled communication path at all.
changes.after: New core/event_bus.py::EventBus -- synchronous in-process publish(topic, payload)/subscribe(topic, handler), plus a '*' wildcard subscription so the GUI (or History Manager, or anything else) can listen to everything without knowing every topic name in advance. A bad subscriber can never break the publisher or other subscribers (each handler call is wrapped in try/except). A capped history buffer (recent(limit, topic)) lets any late subscriber (e.g. a GUI panel that opens after the run started) catch up. Wired at the structural level: pipeline/pipeline.py::Pipeline now publishes 'pipeline.<step_name>.started/completed/failed' around every step automatically (Collector/Parser/RuleEngine/Scorer/AI/Report steps all get this for free, no per-step edits needed -- this covers the full Collector->Parser->Rule->Export chain from the goal), and engine/collector.py additionally publishes 'collector.started'/'collector.completed'/'collector.failed' at the job level. Job Manager and History Manager both publish their own lifecycle events onto the same bus, so 'GUI' just needs one subscribe('*', ...) call to see everything end-to-end.
changes.validated: Manually verified: subscribed a wildcard listener, ran a 2-step pipeline where the second step raised an exception -- observed the exact expected event sequence (stepA.started, stepA.completed, stepB.started, stepB.failed) with the exception still propagating normally to the caller. Also verified collector.started/collector.completed fire correctly around a full collect_all() run.

validation.history_complete: Archival captures raw CLI logs, config snapshots, and reports (all already inside runs/<run_id>/ per the pre-existing RunManager layout) plus job-correlated structured logs (new in this phase), moved as one unit into archive/ per customer/profile/run(job). list_history() gives one combined, correctly-ordered view of active + archived runs.
validation.job_manager_stable: Verified real queueing (second submit does not get dropped), cooperative cancellation, and resume-from-cancelled-or-failed across multiple manual test runs with no crashes or state corruption.
validation.event_bus_implemented: Verified topic-based and wildcard subscription, exception isolation between subscribers, and automatic instrumentation of every pipeline step plus the collector's job-level lifecycle -- satisfies 'everything communicates through events, no direct coupling' at the stage-transition level (Collector/Parser/Rule/Scorer/AI/Report steps and Job/History lifecycle), though see architecture review below for where direct coupling still remains.
manual_tests_run: core/event_bus.py: topic + wildcard subscription, publish with a broken handler (must not raise)
core/job_manager.py: submit two same-kind jobs (real queueing), cancel mid-run, resume from CANCELLED
core/history_manager.py: create_run -> finish_run -> archive_completed_run -> list_history round trip against a real customer/profile (data/acme/siteA)
pipeline/pipeline.py: Event Bus events fire correctly around a passing and a failing step
engine/collector.py: collector.started/completed fire correctly around a full 7-device mocked collection run

architecture_review.layering_today: core/ (cross-cutting: event_bus, job_manager, history_manager, progress_engine, structured_log, worker_pool, storage_service, paths, context, finding) -> engine/ (domain logic: collector, run_manager, profile_manager, device_inventory, comparator, scorer, history) -> plugins/ (vendor + parser plugin registries) -> rule_engine/ (rule plugin registry + evaluation) -> pipeline/ (step orchestration) -> api/ (pywebview-facing mixins) -> gui_web.py (composition root). This is a reasonably clean layered dependency direction (api -> pipeline -> engine/plugins/rule_engine -> core), confirmed by this phase's changes fitting in without needing to reverse any dependency.
strengths: Plugin registries (plugins/parsers, plugins/vendors, rule_engine/registry) are genuinely decoupled -- adding a vendor or rule requires zero edits to pipeline/steps.py, confirmed in Phase 3.

engine/run_manager.py's Run state machine (READY/RUNNING/PAUSED/FAILED/ABORTED/COMPLETED with resume/retry/crash-recovery) was already production-grade before this phase -- Job Manager deliberately did not duplicate it, only added a general-purpose queueing/cancellation layer on top.

Event Bus integration required editing exactly 2 files (pipeline.py, collector.py) to instrument the entire Collector->Parser->Rule->Scorer->AI->Report chain, because Pipeline's existing on_step hook point already existed in the right place -- a sign the Phase 1-2 step abstraction was designed well.
remaining_direct_coupling: pipeline/steps.py::ParserStep/RuleEngineStep/ScorerStep still pass data between each other via ctx.data[...] dict keys (collected_vlan, verdicts_by_stage, etc.) rather than via Event Bus payloads -- the Event Bus wraps this pipeline as an *observer* (for logging/GUI/History), it does not replace the actual data flow between steps. A fully event-driven pipeline (where ParserStep subscribes to a 'collector.completed' event instead of receiving ctx directly) would be a larger, riskier change and was judged out of scope here -- Pipeline.run()'s direct ctx-passing loop is unchanged.

api/grade_api.py now has two parallel entrypoints (run_grade() synchronous, run_grade_async() via JobManager) -- this is intentional (avoid breaking existing GUI wiring) but is itself a form of duplication that should be resolved once the GUI is migrated fully onto the async path.

core/history_manager.py infers 'the run that was just created' via run_manager.list_runs(...)[0] (newest by run_id) rather than receiving an explicit run_id/RunHandle -- correct because collect_all() creates exactly one run per invocation, but fragile if that invariant ever changes (e.g. concurrent grading runs against the same profile).

known_gaps: Job Manager's cancellation is cooperative only -- a fn that doesn't check job.cancel_requested (e.g. the current grading job body, which calls main.grade_via_pipeline() as one opaque call) cannot actually be interrupted mid-flight yet. Making engine/collector.py's per-command loop check a cancel token would close this; not done in this pass to limit blast radius on the just-stabilized Phase 4 collector changes.

Event Bus is in-process/synchronous only -- no persistence, no cross-process delivery. Acceptable for the current single-process pywebview app; would need rework if AutoCheck ever became multi-process/distributed.

The GUI (web_ui/js/*.js) still polls via setInterval rather than subscribing to the Event Bus -- this phase makes the server side fully event-driven, but actually pushing those events to the browser-side JS (pywebview has no native server-push without window.evaluate_js plumbing) remains unimplemented, same gap flagged in PHASE4_MIGRATION_REPORT.json.

History Manager only handles the customer/profile/run tree (data/<customer>/<profile>/runs -> archive). The legacy labs/<project_id>/ tree (grading-mode projects without a customer/profile identity) has no equivalent archival -- its raw_logs/config_snapshots/report_latest.md are never moved to any archive location. This mirrors the pre-existing 'two parallel data-root trees' issue noted in Phase 3/4 research and was not resolved here.

engine/history.py's per-lab-name scored-JSON store and the new customer/profile/run history are two separate, non-integrated 'history' concepts with overlapping names -- a future phase should either merge them or rename one to avoid confusion.
technical_debt_master_list: Only 'arista' has registered parsers in plugins/parsers/registry.py -- devices marked vendor: cisco silently produce no structured data (Phase 3 gap, still open).

core/parsed_device.py::ParsedDevice is defined but unused -- collected_vlan/collected_stp/collected_extended dicts remain the live data-passing contract between ParserStep and RuleEngineStep (Phase 3 gap, still open).
Parser cache (plugins/parsers/cache.py) is in-memory/per-process only, cleared on restart (Phase 3 gap, still open).
report/textfsm_parsers/*.py is a separate, uncoordinated parsing path used only by report/textfsm_parser.py -- never reconciled with the plugin parser registry (Phase 3 gap, still open).

run_grade() (api/grade_api.py) is still fully synchronous for the original code path; run_grade_async() (this phase) is additive, not a replacement -- GUI needs a follow-up migration to fully retire the blocking path (Phase 4 gap, partially addressed this phase via the new async path, not yet fully closed).
logs/structured_<date>.jsonl has no rotation/retention policy (Phase 4 gap, still open).
ProgressEngine's ETA is a naive linear extrapolation from average per-device duration -- inaccurate for jobs with uneven per-device timing (Phase 4 gap, still open, low priority/cosmetic).
GUI (web_ui/js/*.js) still polls via setInterval; no push/event-stream reaches the browser despite the server now being fully event-driven (Phase 4 gap, restated and still open after Phase 5).
Job Manager cancellation is cooperative-only and the current grading job body is one opaque call that cannot yet check a cancel token mid-run (new gap, this phase).
Two parallel data-root trees (labs/<project_id>/ legacy vs data/<customer>/<profile>/) remain unreconciled; History Manager (this phase) only covers the new tree (new/restated gap, this phase).
engine/history.py (per-lab scored-JSON diffing) and the new customer/profile/run History Manager are two separate 'history' concepts with no integration and overlapping naming (new gap, this phase).

api/job_runner.py (the older idle/running/done/error, one-slot-per-kind mechanism used by log-analysis jobs) and api/terminal_inspection_api.py's bespoke cancel flag were not migrated onto core/job_manager.py in this pass -- three job-tracking mechanisms now coexist (JobRunner, terminal_inspection's ad-hoc flag, and the new JobManager) rather than one. A follow-up phase should consolidate all job-like work onto JobManager.
